issues.reason: Dual-emit is mandatory beside a reified state ('keep the flat copular atom (dual-emit as always)'), and over a plural group that flat half is the per-member property atom in the rule's conclusion (the Resultatives plural clause; 'a universal over a COPULAR predicate ... a rule whose conclusion is the property atom'), so omitting (Member $x visible) leaves the plain 'is this marker visible?' question unbindable, which is the exact failure dual-emit exists to prevent.

gaps_confirmed: No listed reification trigger licenses turning the stative trigger clause 'the tide is low' into the premise eventuality that the consequent's During link requires; the whenever machinery is illustrated only with a verbal trigger clause.

The bare 'when P, Q' routing covers generic/indefinite participants (the rule form) and definite participants in a one-off narrative (two plain ordered events), but not definite participants in a present-tense genuine regularity, which is this sentence.
defect_summary: The compliant form keeps the per-occurrence reified state and adds the flat half as one more conjunct of the same consequent - (Member $x visible) beside (Member (sk_visible $s $x) visible), (Experiencer ...), (During ...) and (Below ...) - which the plural-group flat-half rule explicitly licenses, so this defect does have a licensed fix.
notes: Everything else is licensed: the definite-plural group witness, grave_marker with the head genus emitted and the noun modifier suppressed, the top-level definite typings, the sk_* premise constants (each asserted at top level), and Below as the surface preposition actually used, attached to the state witness as an event-side oblique.
